doc.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Drugs and alcohol among jazz musicians
summary: Zeitlin explains how the itinerant life and performance pressure lead to drug use, and doubts Charlie Parker's creativity came from heroin.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: How could you prove that? You’d have to subject someone — I don’t know, I can’t imagine how you would run a test to see if that — well one last question kind of on that subject — throughout jazz it’s unfortunately been a lot of musicians connected with drug abuse and alcohol and so forth. Is there a reason for that other than the fact that a lot of times they make their living in bars and so forth. But is there other things that would make that come to pass?

I think there are other factors other than just the access and the social pressure of being part of a certain culture and to be like other people and the emulation of idols if they’re using then you want to use as you are coming up. But I think the life itself, the nomadic, itinerant life, plus the pressures of standing up in front of an audience and doing an emotional strip tease night after night, for some people that’s really quite threatening and taking various kinds of drugs may make it easier for them to get into that space. And I’ve known people, because of their own particular psychology, that clearly play better when they’re on their drug of choice. And I’ve known people who, you know feel anxious and take the drug but then it erodes their sense of form so markedly when they play that what happens in that there’s a lot of heat but not much light in their music. So I think there’s quite a spectrum of people in terms of how they use their drugs. And for some people it really clearly seems to be adaptive for them. And for others it actually impedes their music.

Yeah. I remember reading certain opinions about Charlie Parker that he would not have been able to play what he did if he had not been on heroin or something. And I hate to believe that. I just simply don’t want to believe that, that that’s where that creativity comes from.

Oh I don’t think it comes from that. Again, I don’t know how really the details psychologically of how he was put together. I mean if he were one of these people who was just so anxious or so internally conflicted that he needed some drug to at least stop
that process long enough to be able to tap into his creativity, then maybe it did facilitate the work. For the large majority of people, in my experience, it’s been an impediment.
